subject: building
clues: flat, toy-like colours; windows don't line up
explanation: Too smooth and too perfect: plastic-looking surfaces, glossy colours and studio light everywhere are common signs of AI.

subject: sms-casual
content: Hi there! I hope this message finds you well. I wanted to let you know that I will be arriving at approximately 6:00 PM this evening. Looking forward to seeing you!
clues: 'I hope this message finds you well' is email language; 'approximately 6:00 PM'
explanation: Nobody texts a friend like a business email. Formal phrases are a big AI tell.

subject: sms-casual
content: What a wonderful day it has been! The weather was absolutely perfect for our picnic, and I'm so grateful we got to spend it together. Let's make more memories like this soon! ☀️🧺
clues: over-the-top positive; 'make more memories'; neat emoji pair
explanation: Gushing, greeting-card language with neat emoji at the end is typical of AI.

subject: sms-casual
content: Just a quick reminder that the book club meeting is tomorrow at 7 PM. Please bring your copy and any thoughts you'd like to share. See you there!
clues: sounds like a group announcement, very complete
explanation: Real friends rarely spell everything out this neatly. It reads like a notice, not a text.

subject: sms-casual
content: Hey! I just tried that new café on the corner and it was amazing. The coffee was rich and smooth, and the pastries were so fresh. You definitely have to check it out!
clues: reads like a review; 'rich and smooth'; no café name
explanation: Descriptions that sound like a review, but name nothing, are a sign of AI.

subject: sms-casual
content: No worries at all! Take your time, there's absolutely no rush. Just let me know whenever you're ready and we can figure out the details then.
clues: very reassuring, repeats itself; no detail
explanation: AI tends to over-reassure ('no worries', 'no rush', 'whenever'). Real people say it once.

subject: sms-casual
content: lol I totally forgot about that! thanks for reminding me, I'll grab it on my way home
clues: casual but every word spelled correctly; vague 'that' and 'it'
explanation: Casual tone with perfect spelling, and no clue what 'it' is, can point to AI.

subject: sms-casual
content: Can't make it tonight unfortunately, something came up at work. Rain check for next week?
clues: natural and short; 'unfortunately' is a little formal
explanation: This could easily be a real person. Neat, polite cancellations are a weak AI clue.

subject: sms-casual
content: omw! traffic's not too bad so should be there in 15ish
clues: uses 'omw' and '15ish'; very human style
explanation: AI can copy text-speak like 'omw' when asked. Style alone can fool you.

subject: sms-casual
content: did u see the match last night?? cant believe that last minute goal
clues: missing apostrophe and double '??' look human; no team named
explanation: Looks human, but notice it never says which match or team. AI often stays vague.

subject: sms-casual
content: my mum's asking if you want the leftover lasagne, she made way too much again haha
clues: family detail and 'again haha' feel real
explanation: Small family details are easy for AI to invent. A believable story isn't proof.

subject: sms-casual
content: running late sorry!! bus just didn't show up. 10 mins
clues: short, rushed, double '!!'
explanation: Very hard: rushed messages are easy to imitate. When in doubt, think about who would really send it.

subject: sms-casual
content: u still got my charger? need it back before thurs x
clues: 'u', 'thurs', 'x': perfect imitation of texting
explanation: When AI is told to text casually, it can look exactly like a person. That's why we check who sent it, not just how it's written.

subject: sms-casual
content: ok so the shop was out of the oat milk, got the almond one instead hope thats fine
clues: everyday detail, missing apostrophe, no punctuation at the end
explanation: Even small 'mistakes' can be generated on purpose. There may be no visible clue at all.

subject: sms-casual
content: gonna be at the pub from 8, come by if ur free
clues: short, casual, nothing unusual
explanation: Some AI messages are impossible to tell apart. That's an important lesson: don't trust a message just because it 'sounds human'.

subject: sms-casual
content: Ahh thank you!! Honestly needed that today. Coffee on me next time
clues: warm and short; capital letters and tidy grammar but natural
explanation: Nothing here gives it away. Being unsure is the right answer sometimes.

subject: delivery
content: DHL Express: Customs duty of £2.49 is due for your parcel GB4471. Pay within 48h or it will be returned: dhl-customs-pay.com
clues: small 'customs' fee; the link is not dhl.com
explanation: Small fees are used so you don't think twice. Couriers' real sites are their own domains, not 'dhl-customs-pay.com'.

subject: account
content: Netflix: We're having trouble with your current billing information. Please update your details to keep watching: netflix-account-help.net
clues: real brand name; urgent tone; look-alike link
explanation: Using a real brand makes scams believable. Always update payments inside the app you already use.

subject: family
content: Dad it's me, I'm using a friend's phone, mine fell in the river 😩 Can you send £180 for a new one? I'll pay you back Friday. Don't call, can't talk right now
clues: unknown number; asks for money; 'don't call'
explanation: 'Don't call me' is the big red flag. A real child would be happy for you to call their friend's phone.

subject: bank
content: Lloyds Bank: Did you attempt a payment of £1,240.00 to M. Patel? If NOT, call our fraud team immediately on 020 7946 0018.
clues: real bank name and fraud wording; but gives its OWN number to call
explanation: Scammers include a phone number so you call them. Only call the number on the back of your card.

subject: tax
content: GOV.UK: Our records show you overpaid tax in 2025. You are due a refund of £214.80. Claim online before 30/10: gov-uk-taxrefund.com
clues: looks official; deadline; link isn't on gov.uk
explanation: Real government sites end in '.gov.uk'. 'gov-uk-taxrefund.com' is a different website.

subject: job
content: Hi, I'm Laura from a recruitment agency. Your profile matches a part-time remote role (£120-£350/day). Can I message you on WhatsApp with details?
clues: friendly and specific; you never applied; moves you to WhatsApp
explanation: Job scams start friendly and move you to WhatsApp. Real recruiters don't promise big daily pay for unknown roles.

subject: delivery
content: Evri: We tried to deliver your parcel today but no one was home. Choose a new delivery slot: evri.redeliver-parcel.com
clues: very normal wording; a real courier name; the domain is 'redeliver-parcel.com'
explanation: Read the link backwards: the real website is the last part before '.com'. Here that's 'redeliver-parcel', not Evri.

subject: account
content: Apple: Your Apple ID was used to sign in on a new iPhone near Manchester. If this wasn't you, lock your account here: apple-id-support-centre.com
clues: realistic security alert; link to a fake 'support' site
explanation: Real security alerts ask you to open Settings yourself. Never follow a link in a security text.

subject: bank
content: Your card ending 4821 has been temporarily frozen due to unusual activity. To unfreeze, reply with your date of birth and postcode.
clues: no link at all, but asks for personal details by text
explanation: Banks never ask for your details by text reply. Personal info can be used to steal your identity.

subject: shopping
content: Amazon: Your order #204-5541 for Apple AirPods Pro (£229.00) has been confirmed. If you did not place this order, call 0808 157 0192 to cancel.
clues: an order you didn't make, designed to scare you into calling
explanation: Fake 'order confirmations' make you panic and call. Check your orders in the real app instead.

subject: appointment
content: Hi, this is Greenfield Vets. Biscuit is due her annual booster. Call us on the usual number or book online to arrange.
clues: from a place you know; uses your pet's name; no link
explanation: A reminder that knows your pet and asks nothing is almost certainly real.

subject: shopping
content: Thanks for shopping at Hilltop Hardware. Your receipt is in the app. Questions? Pop in or call the store.
clues: after a purchase you made; no payment or link
explanation: Receipts for something you just bought, that ask for nothing, are normal.

subject: family
content: Mum, train's delayed 20 mins, don't wait for me for dinner. Love you
clues: from a saved contact; no request
explanation: Messages from saved family numbers that ask for nothing are safe.

subject: code
content: Your Uber code: 7741. Never share this code. Didn't request it? You can ignore this message.
clues: a code you just asked for; tells you not to share
explanation: Genuine login codes always say 'never share'. Only use one you requested yourself.

subject: delivery
content: Your parcel was delivered at 14:12 and left in your safe place (porch). Photo in the app.
clues: delivery confirmation with no link or fee
explanation: A confirmation that just tells you what happened, with no link, is a normal update.

subject: travel
content: TrainLine: Your 08:45 to Leeds is running about 15 minutes late. We're sorry for the delay.
clues: matches a trip you booked; nothing to click
explanation: Travel updates for a journey you booked, with nothing to click, are genuine.

subject: account
content: You've signed in to Spotify on a new device: Chrome on Windows. If this wasn't you, go to your account settings to change your password.
clues: security alert, but no link, points to settings
explanation: Security alerts can be real. The safe ones send you to settings yourself, not to a link.

subject: bank
content: Barclays: You've set up a new payee 'J SMITH'. If you didn't do this, call us on the number on the back of your card.
clues: real bank name and a payee warning, but tells you to use your card's number
explanation: Looks scary, but it's the right advice: use the number on your card, not one in a text.

subject: delivery
content: Royal Mail: We have a parcel for you with £3.10 to pay. A grey card has been left at your address with how to pay.
clues: mentions a fee (scam-like), but points to a card at your door, not a link
explanation: Some real deliveries do have fees. The safe sign is that it doesn't ask you to pay through a link.

subject: job
content: Hi, it's Priya from BrightPath Recruitment, we spoke on Tuesday. The interview with Northside Ltd is confirmed for Mon 10am. I'll email the details.
clues: refers to a conversation you had; no money, no WhatsApp
explanation: This sounds like a job scam at first, but it follows up on a real conversation and asks for nothing.

subject: tax
content: HMRC: Your tax return for 2025-26 is due by 31 January. Sign in to your account at gov.uk to complete it.
clues: a tax text without a link, pointing to gov.uk
explanation: Tricky: tax texts feel scammy, but this one only tells you to visit gov.uk yourself.

subject: bank
content: Monzo: Your card ending 7731 was declined at FreshMart because it's frozen. Unfreeze it in the app if this was you.
clues: card warning, but sends you to the app, asks for nothing
explanation: Very hard: card warnings look like scams, but this one only tells you to use your own app.

subject: code
content: Your WhatsApp code: 312-889. Don't share this code with others.
clues: short and bare; looks like the codes scammers ask for
explanation: Codes are real when YOU asked for one. Scammers ask you to forward codes, so never send them on.

subject: family
content: Hi it's Tom's new number! Old phone finally died. Save this one 👍
clues: unknown 'new number' (a scam trick), but asks for nothing
explanation: This looks like the 'Hi Mum' scam, but it asks for nothing. Check by calling the old number before you save it.

subject: appointment
content: NHS: Your appointment at St Mary's Outpatients is on 4 Nov at 09:20. To cancel or change, call the number on your letter.
clues: official NHS name and details; no link; refers to your letter
explanation: Health appointment texts are real when they match a letter you have and contain no links.
